<reason>Both sides were disciplined and the clash narrowed properly, but A built the cleaner comparative path. A owned the incidence frame ("designed to transfer wealth upward"), which B largely conceded and could only reframe around purchasing power. A's two best moves were comparative rather than merely assertive: (1) the crisis reversal — an uncapped subsidy is precisely the instrument that collapses abruptly in a fiscal shock, while cash is a defended line item with named recipients — which B answered only glancingly ("neither identifies missing households nor guarantees purchasing power"); and (2) the closing turn on B's own audit trigger, showing that the 95%/six-month/30-day standard is pointed exclusively at the reform, would be failed outright by the subsidy, and demands exactly the verification capacity B says divided states lack. That last point bites hardest in Libya-type cases, where B's counterplan leaves a smuggling-funded regressive transfer running indefinitely. B's route stayed live: the "we proceed" concession genuinely exposes what the deadline uniquely adds, and the indirect pass-through / unregistered worker objection was well pressed. But A had a real answer (near-universal payments, as with Iran and Saudi compensation), which reduces B's harm story from "families uncompensated" to "savings are smaller" — a weaker complaint, especially since A explicitly ranked protection first and fiscal savings as residual. B's closing defence of asymmetry rests on status-quo bias that A had already destabilised. A also incurred a real execution cost: in Rebuttal 2 it accused B of "saying nothing" and dodging, when B structurally could not yet have answered, and cited a nonexistent reference id. B answered its pressure questions honestly with clean A1:/A2: labels. That keeps the margin narrow rather than solid.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's closing turn on B's own test: applying B's 95%-of-poor-households, appeals-in-thirty-days audit standard to the fuel subsidy itself, which has no recipients and no appeals process at all, exposing the test as a one-directional veto that also presupposes the very state capacity B claims is missing.</best_rebuttal>
